**Triage (R+26)** — graded `pm:queue` · `domain:ui` · `priority:p2` · type `Task`.

**Lands in:** `packages/fields/src/index.tsx` (`buildValidationRules`) ⇒ published library ⇒ `domain:ui`.

**Type `Task`, ⛔ not `Bug`:** the card asserts **no defect for any specific type**, and it is right not to. "The shared producer has no branch" is a fact; whether that is *reachable* depends per type on whether a widget can hold a spec-refusing stored value and present it for re-save. `location` had that property; `address` may not. ⇒ the deliverable is a **survey**, and a survey is a `Task`.

**p2:** nothing is claimed broken, and the one measured member (#6744) came back with a zero violation count.

## ⛔ Scope — ratifying the card's own fence, which is the important half

The card fences itself twice and triage is making both binding rather than advisory:

1. ⛔ **This is not a request to add branches.** #6744 landed **only** because a hard precondition — a count of existing violating values — came back zero within measurable scope. ⇒ every class here needs **its own count before its own disposition**.
2. ⭐ The card's sharpest line, and the reason this must not be dispatched as "do what #6744 did, seven more times":

> Reproducing #6744's shape N times without N counts is precisely the **migration-shaped consequence** that ruling was written to prevent.

⇒ **deliverable = the two readings per class**, (a) does a widget render and re-emit a stored value of that type unchanged, and (b) how many spec-refusing values of that type exist in measurable datasets. ⛔ No branch is added in this card, for any type.

⚠️ **Conditional escalation, registered now rather than discovered later:** a **non-zero** count for any class does **not** convert into queue work. It escalates to the same *warn-or-block plus a repair path* product decision the #6744 ruling named — that touches existing deployed data shape, which is a manual floor. ⇒ ⛔ stop and file a `needs-user-decision` card per affected class; do not choose a posture in the PR.

⇒ each class then becomes independently dispatchable **or closable on its own evidence**, which is the outcome that makes this survey worth its slot.

⭐ **Dedup accepted as sound, ⛔ not re-run.** `/search/issues` is 403 for that seat, so it used a repo-scoped REST listing of 251 open issues plus a local grep — zero hits for `valueSchemaFor` / `validation coverage` / `ADR-0104` — and **reverse-checked the zero with a control that must hit** (`location` in title → #6744). It also checked the nearest neighbour #2731 and correctly rejected it as a duplicate: that is a `domain:spec` card about declaring value shapes in the spec, a different layer from this renderer-side producer. ⇒ a zero with a control under it, which is the standard.

**Provenance:** filed under #6744's ruling (「全字段类型的存量校验覆盖普查是另一张卡,发现即另立」) ⇒ the split is already ruled. ⛔ Do not fold back into #6744 (`pm:dispatched`).

# Survey — the two readings per ADR-0104 value-shape class

Base `30266cf` (objectui `main`). ⛔ **No branch was added to `buildValidationRules` for any type**, per the fence this card sets and triage made binding. No PR; the probe used below was a read-only measurement and is deleted.

## The instrument — #6744's, reused rather than reinvented

Every verdict below comes from `valueSchemaFor(def, 'stored')` in `@objectstack/spec/data` — the same schema the engine's record validator checks a stored value against under ADR-0104 D1. ⛔ No bound, key set or id shape is restated on this side.

⭐ One version fact worth stating, because it makes both repos' datasets comparable: objectui resolves `@objectstack/spec@17.2.0`, and objectstack's workspace `packages/spec` is also **17.2.0**. One build of the contract adjudicated everything here.

The classes `valueSchemaFor` declares a shape for, and the widget each resolves to (`fieldWidgetMap` + `field-type-alias.ts`):

| class | spec shape (stored) | widget |
|---|---|---|
| `address` | `AddressValueSchema` | `AddressField` |
| `composite` / `record` | `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` | `ObjectField` |
| `repeater` | `z.array(z.record(...))` | `GridField` |
| `vector` | `z.array(z.number())` | `VectorField` |
| `lookup` / `master_detail` / `tree` | `ReferenceIdValueSchema` | `LookupField` |
| `user` | `ReferenceIdValueSchema` | `UserField` |
| `file` / `video` / `audio` | `FileReferenceIdValueSchema` | `FileField` |
| `image` | `FileReferenceIdValueSchema` | `ImageField` |
| `avatar` | `FileReferenceIdValueSchema` | `AvatarField` |

---

# Reading (a) — does a widget hold a spec-refusing stored value and present it for re-save?

**Measured, not read off the source.** A real `ObjectForm` in `mode: 'edit'` was seeded with a stored value the spec refuses, then submitted **without touching the control** — the same shape #6744 used. Recorded per class: what the widget showed, whether `dataSource.update` ran, whether the written value is byte-identical to the stored one, and whether anything set `aria-invalid`.

**Result: yes for all 14 classes. Every one wrote the refused value back unchanged, with nothing marked invalid.**

| class | seeded refused value | what the widget showed | update | written value | invalid |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | `'1 Main St, Seattle WA'` (flat string) | 5 sub-inputs, **all empty** | called | identical | no |
| `composite` | `'{"width":10,"height":20}'` (JSON text) | the raw JSON text | called | identical | no |
| `record` | `[{ name: 'A' }]` (array) | the raw JSON text | called | identical | no |
| `repeater` | `{ '0': { a: 1 } }` (index-keyed object) | one row, `#1` + `Add line` | called | identical | no |
| `vector` | `['0.12','0.34']` (numeric strings) | `[0.1200, 0.3400...](2D)` — formats the **strings** as if numbers | called | identical | no |
| `lookup` | `'{"id":"acc_1","name":"Northwind"}'` (embedded record text) | **`Northwind`** — it hydrates the embedded record and shows its name | called | identical | no |
| `master_detail` | `'{"id":"p_1"}'` | `p_1` | called | identical | no |
| `user` | `{ id: 'u_1', name: 'Ada' }` (expanded object) | **`AD` avatar + `Ada`** | called | identical | no |
| `tree` | `'[{"id":"c_1"}]'` | `Select…` (nothing) | called | identical | no |
| `file` | `'https://cdn.example.com/report.pdf'` | **`report.pdf`**, parsed out of the URL | called | identical | no |
| `image` | `{ url: '…/a.png', name: 'a.png' }` (legacy inline blob) | its add-more affordance | called | identical | no |
| `avatar` | `'https://cdn.example.com/av.png'` | initials + `Change Avatar` | called | identical | no |
| `video` | `'https://cdn.example.com/a.mp4'` | `a.mp4` | called | identical | no |
| `audio` | `'https://cdn.example.com/a.mp3'` | `a.mp3` | called | identical | no |
| **`location` (CONTROL)** | `{ lat: 999, lng: 999 }` | `999, 999` in the input | **0 calls** | — | **`aria-invalid="true"`** |

⭐ **The control is the load-bearing row.** `location` is the one class with a branch (#6744), and in the same harness, same run, it blocks the write and marks the control invalid. So the fourteen "wrote it back" readings are a property of those classes, not an artifact of a harness that cannot see a refusal.

**Second control direction.** For seven classes a spec-**accepted** value was seeded as well (`address` `{street,city}`, `composite` `{width:10}`, `record` `{primary:{…}}`, `repeater` `[{a:1}]`, `vector` `[0.12,0.34]`, `file` `'file_abc123'`, `image` `'img_abc123'`): written back unchanged, nothing invalid — identical outcome to the refused values. ⇒ the surface makes **no distinction whatsoever** between a value the platform accepts and one it refuses. That is the "no branch" fact, measured rather than inferred.

⚠️ Two rows deserve reading twice, because they are worse than the plain "unchanged re-save" the card anticipated:

- `lookup` and `user` **hydrate the refusing value into a friendly label** (`Northwind`, `Ada`). To the person on the form the field looks correctly filled; the stored value is an embedded record the write path refuses under ADR-0104 D1.
- `file` / `video` / `audio` **derive a filename from the legacy URL** (`report.pdf`, `a.mp4`), so a retired external-URL value presents as a real attachment.
- `address` is the opposite failure: it presents **nothing** (five empty boxes) and still re-saves the original string. ⇒ the card's hypothesis "`address` may not [have the property]" is **falsified**: it does re-emit unchanged; it just never shows the user what it is about to re-save.

---

# Reading (b) — how many spec-refusing values of each class exist in measurable datasets?

**Answer: zero refused, in every class — but the population differs by three orders of magnitude between classes, so the zeros are not worth the same and are reported per class.**

## Population and how it was bounded

Values were adjudicated only where the field's **definition** could be identified — never by bare key name (a global key match is unusable here: field names like `record`, `user`, `avatar`, `gallery` collide with ordinary property names, and the first pass produced 20,229 "values" of which 10,727 "refused", every sampled one a CSS style object, a Mongo filter operator or a view-type string). Three precise joins:

- **J1 — objectstack seeds.** Every `defineSeed(Object, { records })` call, joined through the file's imports to that object module's own `fields` map: **24 of 24 calls joined, 0 unjoined**. Generated rows (`...Array.from(…)` inside an arrow body) are walked too.
- **J2 — same-document schema+data.** A `fields` map/array plus a sibling value container (`data` / `defaultValues` / `records` / `rows` / …) inside one file. Run over **10,516 files across both repos**.
- **J3 — the qa/dogfood field-zoo matrix**, whose entries carry their own `type`.

Dataset files parsed: **875** (400 under objectstack `examples/` + `packages/qa/`, 475 under objectui `examples/`), inside the 10,516-file J2 sweep. Datasets covered: the app-showcase seed, app-crm, app-todo, embed-objectql, `packages/qa` (dogfood incl. the field-zoo matrix), and the objectui schema-catalog — i.e. #6744's three, plus every other example app.

## Controls — 32 of them, in the same execution, through the same call path

For each class, one value that **must be accepted** and one that **must be refused** were adjudicated by the same `schemaFor()` used for the readings: **32/32 behaved as required** (e.g. `file` accepts `'file_1'` and refuses `'https://cdn.example.com/a.pdf'`; `lookup` accepts `'acc_1'` and refuses `'{"id":"acc_1"}'`; the `location` pair from #6744 reproduces). ⇒ each zero below is a reading, not a query that silently matched nothing.

## Per class

| class | values adjudicated | refused | where the population comes from | how much the zero is worth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lookup` | **76** | **0** | showcase seed 45, app-crm 31 | substantive — comparable to #6744's 28 |
| `master_detail` | **36** | **0** | showcase seed 36 | substantive |
| `vector` | 4 | 0 | showcase 1, ui-catalog 2, dogfood 1 | thin |
| `address` | 2 | 0 | showcase 1, dogfood 1 | thin **and structurally weak — see below** |
| `composite` | 2 | 0 | showcase 1, dogfood 1 | thin, schema is near-open |
| `record` | 2 | 0 | showcase 1, dogfood 1 | thin, schema is near-open |
| `repeater` | 2 | 0 | showcase 1, dogfood 1 | thin |
| `file` | 1 | 0 | dogfood matrix (`file_zoo_doc`) | **N=1** |
| `image` | 1 | 0 | dogfood matrix (`file_zoo_image`) | **N=1** |
| `avatar` | 1 | 0 | dogfood matrix (`file_zoo_avatar`) | **N=1** |
| `video` | 1 | 0 | dogfood matrix (`file_zoo_video`) | **N=1** |
| `audio` | 1 | 0 | dogfood matrix (`file_zoo_audio`) | **N=1** |
| `user` | **0** | — | nothing anywhere | ⛔ **not a zero reading — no value exists to measure** |
| `tree` | **0** | — | the one dogfood entry is a runtime-resolved placeholder | ⛔ **not a zero reading** |

Total: **129 stored values adjudicated, 0 refused**, plus 3 non-static values (the dogfood matrix's `REFERENCE_PLACEHOLDER` for `f_lookup` / `f_master_detail` / `f_tree`, substituted with a real row id at runtime) reported as **not adjudicable statically** rather than counted either way.

⛔ `user` and `tree` must not be read as "clean". The showcase deliberately leaves `f_user` / `f_users` / `f_owner` unseeded (its own comment: `sys_user` rows come from sign-up, not seeds), and the five file-class fields are unseeded too — `showcase_task.cover` carries a docblock explaining that the ADR-0104 D3 wave-2 stored form is an opaque `sys_file` id, which is why nothing is seeded there. **The classes most likely to hold a legacy shape are precisely the ones with almost no measurable values.**

## Independent cross-check (#6744's method B, adapted)

A deliberately **over-inclusive** pass — pair any literal under a key that any field container in the dataset roots declares with that class — was run to see whether the precise joins had missed a record value. 147 hits across the dataset files, **30 refused, every one hand-classified and none of them a stored record value**:

- **25** are i18n label maps: `fields: { account: { label: 'Account' } }` in `system/translations` — refused only because a `{label}` object is not a record id;
- **5** are flow templates: `account: '{account_id}'` in `flows/*.ts` — refused only because `ReferenceIdValueSchema` rejects a leading `{`, and the template is interpolated before it is ever stored.

Extended to both whole repos, every file-class and reference-class refusal falling in a dataset path is likewise a permission matrix (`crm_lead: {allowRead:true}`), an expand spec (`contact: {object, fields}`) or a dashboard filter flag (`customer: false`). The one value the precise joins genuinely missed was `account: 'Northwind'` inside a generated 24-row block — accepted, and now folded into the 76 above.

## ⚠️ Boundary, as #6744's ruling requires it stated

Customer deployments are **not measurable from this container**. Every zero above means "zero within measurable scope", never "does not exist". Nothing here is evidence about deployed data.

## ⭐ One structural result that changes what a zero can mean

`AddressValueSchema` declares **every** member optional and is a zod `z.object`, which **strips** unrecognized keys instead of refusing them. So the only `address` values the stored contract can refuse are non-objects. Measured in the same run: the showcase seed's `{ street, city, state, postal_code, country }` is **accepted**, with `postal_code` silently dropped from the parse output.

⇒ for `address` — and, more weakly, for `composite` / `record`, which are `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` and admit any object — a zero-violation count is **close to unfalsifiable**, and is not evidence that stored values of that class are well-formed. Whatever disposition those three classes get should rest on the schema question, not on their count. (The `postal_code` drift itself is filed separately as objectstack#13388.)

---

# Verification of the three PM assumptions

1. **Branch list re-derived on my own base, not taken from the card.** On `30266cf`, `buildValidationRules` sits at `packages/fields/src/index.tsx:2645` and its branches are, in full: `required` · `minLength`/`maxLength` (each with a legacy snake_case fallback) · `min` · `max` · `pattern` · `email` · `url` · a field-authored `validate` · `location`. ⇒ **unchanged**: none of the four `packages/fields` landings this round (#6811, #6801, #6850, #6858) added or moved a branch, so the survey's subject is the one the card describes.
2. **#6744's instrument read and reused.** Its reading was 28 stored `location` values adjudicated by `valueSchemaFor(…, 'stored')` with controls in the same call, plus a 12,465-file literal sweep whose 44 out-of-range hits were all test fixtures, docblocks, docs prose or changesets. Same predicate, same controls-in-the-same-call discipline, and the same two-method structure used above.
3. **The producer claim is VERIFIED, with one refinement and one boundary.**
   - Verified: `buildValidationRules(field)` at `ObjectForm.tsx:705` and `sectionFields.ts:131` feeds react-hook-form's `Controller`, and the widget's `error` prop is `fieldState.error?.message` at `form.tsx:2683`.
   - Refinement: it is the producer of every rule **except presence** — `form.tsx` deletes the compiled `required` and composes its own live `required` validator (via core's `isMissingForRequired`) so the verdict tracks the record as it changes.
   - ⚠️ Boundary: it is the producer **on the form surface only**. `InlineFieldInput` (detail-page inline editing) never calls it and never receives an `error` prop, so that surface runs no host-side rule at all — including `location`. Filed as **#6868**; this card's readings should be read as bounded to the form surface.

---

# Disposition — no escalation is due

The registered conditional escalation (a non-zero count for any class ⇒ stop, file a `needs-user-decision` card per affected class, do not choose a posture) **did not trigger**: every count is zero. ⛔ No posture was chosen, and no branch was added.

What each class needs before it can be dispatched or closed on its own evidence:

- **`lookup` / `master_detail`** — reading (a) yes; reading (b) 0 of 76 and 0 of 36, the only counts comparable to the precondition #6744 landed on. These two are the ones a "does this class need a branch" decision could actually be taken on today.
- **`file` / `image` / `avatar` / `video` / `audio`** — reading (a) yes, and worse than plain: the widgets present a legacy URL as a named attachment. Reading (b) is **N=1 per class, all id-shaped by construction** in the dogfood matrix. ⛔ That is not yet a count. These classes need a wider population first — and note the stored contract for them narrowed recently (ADR-0104 D3 wave 2), which is exactly the situation where deployed data is most likely to be older than the contract.
- **`user` / `tree`** — no measurable value exists. Any disposition would rest on nothing.
- **`address` / `composite` / `record`** — reading (a) yes; the count cannot falsify much (see above).
- **`repeater` / `vector`** — reading (a) yes; a thin zero (N=2, N=4).

---

## How to reproduce

- Adjudication + controls: a Node script over both repos' dataset files using `valueSchemaFor(def,'stored')` from the resolved `@objectstack/spec@17.2.0`, with the three joins described above. It executes nothing from the datasets; values are read as static literals from the TypeScript/JSON AST.
- Round-trip probe: a vitest file rendering a real `ObjectForm` per class (`packages/plugin-form`), run under the container's shared verify lock — `VERDICT command-exit 0`, 16 tests, 13.3 s. It was never committed and has been removed; `packages/fields` was not touched.
